newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs approve plan to fight AIDS worldwide.
newsitem.headline: MEPs approve plan to fight AIDS worldwide.

text.p: STRASBOURG, Nov 12 (Reuter ) - The European Parliament approved on Tuesday a European Union plan to spend 45 million Ecus over the next three years to fight the spread of AIDS in developing countries.

But to the disappointment of the parliament's development committee, a majority of MEPs rejected the inclusion in the draft regulation of provisions to ensure the money was spent primarily on helping AIDS victims in the poorest countries.
There are 17 million people with AIDS worldwide, over 15 million of whom live in developing countries.

By the turn of the century, the number of AIDS cases is expected to rise to over 40 million, the majority in sub-Saharan Africa where poverty is the main contributing factor to the spread of the epidemic, according to a report by Belgian liberal Anne Andre-Leonard, adopted by MEPs on Tuesday.
British Socialist Glenys Kinnock pointed out in a debate on the proposal on Monday evening that 90 percent of those affected by the disease could not afford the new medicines.
She told Reuters that not concentrating resources on the countries least able to tackle the epidemic was unwise.

But German Christian Democrat Peter Liese argued the EU should have the flexibility to help people in countries like India, Pakistan or Brazil which, although they are not among the poorest nations on the planet, also have huge numbers of destitute people and a devastating AIDS problem.
He pointed out that the parliament had called for a separate "solidarity fund" through which the EU member states could help provide modern forms of treatment for AIDS in the poorest countries.

MEPs have repeatedly expressed disappointment with the limited budget the Council is prepared to allocate to the programme but were told in May by Development Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro that the EU's budget would not stretch to more.

When they approved the Council's common position on the proposal -- COM(95)293 -- MEPs therefore asked for amendments designed to ensure the programme's limited funds are used as efficiently as possible.
These include explicitly promoting condoms as a vital means of AIDS prevention and making the programme less bureaucratic.
"We want people to be able to buy condoms where they are most easily available, not where the Council thinks they should buy them," Liese told Reuters.

Other recommendations stress the need to focus EU action on preventive campaigns targeted at high-risk groups such as street children, refugees and migrant workers, and to teach AIDS prevention in a way which pays more attention to the cultural sensibilities of people in developing countries.
Commissioner Christos Papoutsis told MEPs on Monday the programme was geared towards prevention. This would include cooperation with the pharmaceutical industry to produce the lowest cost medicines.
